introduction: For the past six years, my academic and applied research has focused on gathering, cleaning, analysing, and modelling structured and unstructured data across media, migration, and international development.

I am now transitioning into commercial data analysis, leveraging my experience in defining key questions, validating data integrity, testing hypotheses, and effectively communicating findings. To facilitate this transition, I recently completed a government-funded Data and AI automation bootcamp with The Development Manager and developed the independent projects detailed below, using publicly available data from UK organisations.
opening: I am drawn to the stories behind quantitative data. My journey began in Nigeria, where I studied how rainfall affects rice farms. Since then, I have interviewed newspaper readers, investigated why skilled Nigerians emigrate to the UK, and experimented with artificial intelligence to analyse data more deeply. I'm now looking to apply my experience in a corporate data role.

milestones.title: Spatial Analyst and Real-World Impact
milestones.text: I graduated top of my geography class, achieving first-class honours and straight As in statistics. My final project involved mapping how changes in rainfall affected rice harvests in a specific local government area, combining quantitative analysis with an understanding of real-world consequences.
milestones.note: A strong foundation in geography, statistics, and ArcGIS means I can analyse spatial data to solve real-world challenges.

milestones.title: Academic Excellence & Media Analysis
milestones.text: A Chevening scholarship enabled me to pursue an MSc in Conflict, Statebuilding and Development at the University of Birmingham. My research analysed newspaper coverage and included interviews with readers to examine media framing effects. The findings indicated that biased media coverage influenced readers’ perceptions of conflict actors. I graduated with distinction, achieving 82% for my dissertation, which led my supervisor to recommend that I consider pursuing a PhD.
milestones.note: The Chevening Scholarship is the UK’s highly competitive and prestigious scholarship programme for future global leaders.

milestones.title: Expert in mixed-methods research design and analysis.
milestones.text: My MA in Social Research at the University of Birmingham, supported by ESRC funding, provided training in qualitative and quantitative research design and analysis. This included regression modelling, interviews, and qualitative coding, and I scored 75% in the quantitative module.
milestones.note: I’m comfortable analysing qualitative evidence from interviews, customer feedback and social media, alongside quantitative survey and financial data. I work with structured spreadsheets and databases as well as unstructured text.

milestones.title: Doctoral Research
milestones.text: My doctoral research investigated the emigration of skilled professionals to the UK, combining large-scale computational analysis with qualitative fieldwork. By analysing nearly 29,000 posts from X (formerly Twitter) alongside in-person qualitative interviews, I identified significant discrepancies between public digital sentiment and the underlying motivations expressed in personal narratives. I used Python and Large Language Models (LLMs) to scale text analysis across large unstructured datasets.
milestones.note: I can build Python workflows, use LLMs to analyse large-scale text data, and validate digital sentiment against real-world evidence.

milestones.title: Skilled in Machine Learning
milestones.text: At Oxford’s Spring School in Large Language Models, I studied LLM architecture and configuration. I then evaluated their performance by comparing AI- and human-written code in my research, focusing on discrepancies rather than overlooking them.
milestones.note: I use a human-in-the-loop approach to accelerate analysis with AI while ensuring human oversight identifies and corrects errors. I can easily transfer this skill to an AI-optimistic business.

milestones.title: Transitioning to the Commercial or Public Sector
milestones.text: I completed a competitive, government-funded Data and AI Automation bootcamp and gained core technical skills in analytics and process automation. I then applied these skills to complex public-sector datasets, including council payment reconciliations, to derive actionable operational intelligence. The four projects in this portfolio show my ability to turn vague operational questions into strategic, data-informed recommendations.
milestones.note: I’ve proactively built expertise in modern data tools to strengthen my analytical skills. Beyond writing code, I bring a commercial mindset and a track record of turning analysis into practical business value from day one.

ending.heading: What this means for you
ending.lead: You’d get an analyst who prioritises understanding context and stakeholders over simply focusing on metrics.
points: I’ll disaggregate average figures by region, branch, product or customer group to identify underlying variations before identifying a trend.
I’ll cross-reference quantitative findings with qualitative feedback from customers.
I’ll leverage AI and automation for efficiency gains, while maintaining human oversight to mitigate potential errors.
I’ll present my findings and actionable recommendations in clear, accessible language.

additional_experience: My freelance experience also includes work with Outlier.
